Use this page to understand validation files, execution order and reference matching.

## Organize the validation files

| File                               | Purpose                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `survey-validation.yaml`            | Execution order                |
| `survey-structure-validation.yaml`  | Sheet order and dimensions     |
| `survey-generated-validation.yaml`  | Generated field checks         |
| `survey-business-validation.yaml`   | Custom business checks         |

The process file lists the rules to run against the supplied form model:

```yaml
rulesets:
  structure: survey-structure-validation.yaml
  content:
  - survey-generated-validation.yaml
  - survey-business-validation.yaml
```

Validation runs in this order:

1. Check the form structure. Any structural error or unfinished check blocks content validation.
2. Run generated field checks.
3. Run business checks, even when earlier content checks found problems.

## Read a rule

A rule identifies a field, a check and its parameter:

```yaml
rules:
  field/Observations.count/mandatory: true
  field/Observations.count/type: integer
  field/Observations.count/minimum: 0
  field/Observations.unit/enum: [cm, m]
```

For example, `Observations.count` must be present, contain an integer and be at least zero.

Rules report errors by default. To report a warning instead, supply `value` and `severity` explicitly:

```yaml
rules:
  field/Observations.station/reference: {value: stations, severity: warning}
```

Change generated rules by editing the form model and regenerating them.

For custom R callbacks, follow [Authoring validation rules](rules-authoring.html).

## Interpret the result

| Result             | Meaning                                  |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `result$findings`  | Problems found and their cell locations   |
| `result$execution` | Checks completed, unfinished or failed    |
| `result$complete`  | Whether all required validation completed |
| `result$valid`     | Whether the submission passed validation |

Accept a submission only when `result$complete` and `isTRUE(result$valid)` are both true.

## Accept alternate reference codes

Supply aliases when more than one spelling is explicitly accepted for a code:

```r
references <- list(units = list(values = c("cm", "kg"), aliases = c(CM = "cm")))
```

This accepts `cm`, `kg` and `CM` without changing submitted values. Other spellings remain invalid.

Each alias must point to an existing reference value. A missing reference list leaves the check unfinished.

## Match registry names

Registry matching is exact by default. Enable name matching when case, accents or word order may differ:

```r
index <- registry_index(c("MARTIN Emile", "Jane Smith"), matching = "name",
  aliases = c("J. Smith" = "Jane Smith"))
registry_match_counts(index, c("Emile Martin", "J. Smith", "Unknown"))
# 1 1 0
```

The first two values each match one registry entry; `Unknown` matches none.

A successful match must identify exactly one entry. Multiple matches remain ambiguous.
